findings.title: Handle missing TopicUser row in unsubscribe
State-changing action exposed via GET (CSRF / prefetch toggling)
`unsubscribe_link` translation now requires `unsubscribe_url` for every email with an unsubscribe link
Direct `tu.save!` skips MessageBus publish and notification reason
Client-side unsubscribe route never unsubscribes, but says it did

response: ## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug Title: Handle missing TopicUser row in unsubscribe Affected: - app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105-113 Explanation: `TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns `nil` when the user has no `topic_users` row for the topic. That happens when the user gets emails because they watch the category, are mentioned, or are in a group, without ever visiting the topic. In that case `tu.notification_level` raises `NoMethodError` and the unsubscribe link from the email returns a 500 error. Even when a row exists, `notification_level` can be `nil`. Then `nil > Integer` also raises. Proposed fix: ~~~ruby tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) current = tu.try(:notification_level) || TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] new_level = current > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] ? TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] : TopicUser.notification_levels[:muted] TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: new_level) ~~~ ## 2) Severity: HIGH | Type: Security Title: State-changing action exposed via GET (CSRF / prefetch toggling) Affected: - app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98-116 - config/routes.rb:440-441 Explanation: `unsubscribe` changes the user's notification level on a plain GET request with no token. This causes three problems: - **CSRF:** any third-party page can mute topics for a logged-in victim, e.g. with ``. - **Prefetching:** email clients, link scanners and browser prefetchers will trigger it without the user meaning to. - **Not idempotent:** the action steps the level down on every hit. Watching becomes regular, and a reload (or a second scanner fetch) then mutes the topic. Proposed fix: - Have the GET render a confirmation page only, and do the change via a POST/PUT protected by CSRF. - Or set a fixed target level so repeated hits do not escalate, and use a signed per-user token in the URL. ## 3) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug Title: `unsubscribe_link` translation now requires `unsubscribe_url` for every email with an unsubscribe link Affected: - config/locales/server.en.yml:1852-1855 - lib/email/message_builder.rb:67 Explanation: The shared `unsubscribe_link` string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Only the post notification path in `UserNotifications` passes that value. Other mailers that set `add_unsubscribe_link: true` (digest and other notification types) will not provide it. Examples include the text-body branch of `MessageBuilder` and `html_part`. For those emails, `I18n.t` raises `MissingInterpolationArgument` (Rails default), or a raw `%{unsubscribe_url}` ends up in the email. The spec had to add `unsubscribe_url` just to keep passing, which points to this regression. I can't see those other callers in the diff, so please check them in the repository. Proposed fix: ~~~ruby # keep the generic string and add the topic sentence only when available unsubscribe_link = I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) if @opts[:unsubscribe_url].present? unsubscribe_link << "\n\n" << I18n.t('unsubscribe_link_topic', template_args) end ~~~ ## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug Title: Direct `tu.save!` skips MessageBus publish and notification reason Affected: - app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105-113 Explanation: The action saves the `TopicUser` record directly instead of going through `TopicUser.change`. As a result: - The `notification_level_change` MessageBus event is never published, so the user's other open tabs show a stale state. - `notifications_reason_id` and the related bookkeeping are not updated. Proposed fix: ~~~ruby TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: new_level) ~~~ ## 5) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug Title: Client-side unsubscribe route never unsubscribes, but says it did Affected: - app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:4-10 - app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:5-7 Explanation: The Ember route loads data with `PostStream.loadTopicView`, which calls the normal topic JSON endpoint and not `/unsubscribe`. The level only changes on a full HTML page load. If the user reaches the route through an in-app transition, nothing changes, yet the page still says "You will stop receiving notifications". The message is also inaccurate on a real hit: when the server only moved the user from watching to regular, they may still receive notifications (for example, mentions or replies). Proposed fix: - Make the route's model hook call the unsubscribe endpoint (preferably via a non-GET request). - Word the message based on the level actually returned.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate: TopicUser.find_by returns nil when user has no topic_users row for the topic, causing NoMethodError on tu.notification_level and returning 500 error on unsubscribe
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same issue: TopicUser.find_by can return nil when no record exists, and calling methods on the nil object (tu.notification_level or similar) will cause an error. The golden comment describes it as a 'nil pointer exception' that will 'crash', while the candidate describes it as 'NoMethodError' returning '500 error'. These are the same underlying bug - accessing methods on a potentially nil TopicUser object.

false_positives.candidate: State-changing unsubscribe action exposed via GET request without token, enabling CSRF attacks where third-party pages can mute topics for logged-in users
Email clients, link scanners and browser prefetchers can trigger the unsubscribe action without user intent due to GET exposure
Unsubscribe action is not idempotent - it steps the level down on every hit, so watching becomes regular and a reload then mutes the topic

unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url interpolation, but other mailers using add_unsubscribe_link: true don't provide it, causing MissingInterpolationArgument or raw %{unsubscribe_url} in emails
Direct tu.save! skips MessageBus publish, so notification_level_change event is never published and user's other open tabs show stale state
Direct tu.save! skips notifications_reason_id and related bookkeeping that TopicUser.change would handle
Client-side Ember unsubscribe route calls normal topic JSON endpoint instead of /unsubscribe, so in-app transitions don't actually change notification level
Unsubscribe success message is inaccurate - says user will stop receiving notifications even when server only moved from watching to regular, where they may still receive mentions or replies

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')
